To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetic properties of CoFeZn-Al2O3/Si multilayers are determined by the chemical peculiarities of Si and the inner structure of the magnetic composite layers.

the magnetic properties of CoFeZZr-Al2-03 composite layers and amorphized Si spacers in multilayer nano-structures with a thickness below 5 nm are strongly influenced by the chemical peculiarities of the amorphous Si.
the magnetic and electrical properties of CoFeZn-Al2O3/Si multilayers are controlled by the magnetic phase composition of composite magnetic layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the layer thickness and the chemical composition of silicon on the magnetic and transport properties of multilayer structures.

the effect of chemical peculiarities of the silicon spacers on the magnetic properties of CoFeZZr/Al2O3/Si multilayers, as well as with the possibility of controlling the type and intensity of interlayer magnetic interactions by varying the silicon spacer thickness.
a detailed study of magnetic interactions in multilayer nano-structures with a composite magnetic layer consisting of CoFe and Zr atoms in the form of a solid solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetoresistance effect and magnetic anisotropy are not connected in the investigated nanostructures.
the magnetic phase of the composite layer in nanostructures with amorphous silicon spacers is a ferromagnet with a weakly pronounced uniaxial anisotropy and a small coercive field.
the magnetic and transport properties of the multilayers are determined by both the chemical composition of the magnetic layers and the thickness of the layers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the case of the 35 at % magnetic layer the magnetic properties are mainly determined by the chemical peculiarities of the magnetic phase, and the influence of silicon on the magnetic properties is negligible.

the magnetic properties of the composite layers are determined by the magnetic properties of CoFeZ2r phase, and the magnetic properties of nanostructures are determined by the type of magnetic interaction between the layers.

a high magnetoresistance value is achieved for nanostructures with the lowest layer thicknesses, while a maximum value of the ferromagnetic resonance frequency is obtained for nanostructures with composite layers having the largest thicknesses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic and transport properties of the multilayers can be tuned by varying the thickness of the magnetic layers and the chemical peculiarities of the silicon spacers.
the magnetic phase in the CoFeZr composite layers is inhomogeneous and consists of ferromagnetic CoFe and paramagnetic Zr phases.

the magnetic phase of CoFeZZr-Al2 O3 nanostructure is a ferromagnetic alloy with a Curie temperature of 600 K, and the magnetic properties and ferromagnetic-resonance parameters of nanostructures are determined by the magnetic-phase volume fraction and the magnetic-phase distribution in the layer volume.
